title: AI for work and life: which plan is worth paying for?
dek: 22 services, 14 areas of life and work, and seven models worth comparing. A practical guide to buying a little more possibility.
method: Research-based buying guide using official provider pages, checked September 29, 2026. Recommendations are editorial judgments about task fit, not hands-on benchmarks or an exhaustive market ranking.
disclosure: US dollar list prices before tax where verified. Annual equivalents require annual payment or commitment. Regional offers, usage limits and model availability can change. All shopping links are direct and non-affiliate.

plans.name: ChatGPT
plans.why: Our broad starting point for a mix of writing, analysis, images and building. Free and $8 Go offer lower-cost entry points.
plans.catch: API usage is separate. Higher plans buy access and capacity; they do not make every answer correct. Check which model and limits your tier includes.
plans.alternative: Claude for sustained writing and code; Gemini for Google-centered work.

plans.name: Claude
plans.why: A strong shortlist for document-heavy work, writing and coding. Max tiers start at $100 and $200 monthly when capacity matters.
plans.catch: Fable access on Pro uses paid usage credits; Max has its own allowance rules. A subscription is not an unlimited API account.
plans.alternative: ChatGPT or Gemini before adding another general subscription.

plans.name: Google AI
plans.why: The natural comparison for people living in Gmail, Docs and Sheets. Pro currently bundles 5 TB storage; Ultra starts at $99.99 monthly.
plans.catch: Personal Google AI and business Workspace are different purchases. App access and API billing are separate.
plans.alternative: Use the AI and storage already included in your existing workspace first.

plans.name: Perplexity
plans.why: Worth a look when finding, following and organizing sources is the main job. The search-first interface is the reason to compare it.
plans.catch: A citation is a route to evidence, not proof that the attached sentence is right. Open important sources.
plans.alternative: The web research tools in your existing general assistant.

plans.name: Grok
plans.why: Consider it if the combination of web and X search fits your research habits. Free access makes an initial comparison possible.
plans.catch: The consumer pricing page lists Grok 4.6; do not assume the API’s 4.7 is included in every app tier. Search access still needs source checking.
plans.alternative: Perplexity for source discovery, or a general assistant you already pay for.

plans.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
plans.why: A workspace purchase for teams whose material and daily work already live in Microsoft 365. Integration may matter more than a marginal model preference.
plans.catch: A qualifying base Microsoft 365 license costs extra. The page also advertises promotions; we use the $21 list price rather than the temporary $18 offer.
plans.alternative: Eligible work accounts may already have Copilot Chat; check before upgrading.

plans.name: Cursor
plans.why: An editor-centered way to keep AI close to code, context and changes. Pay for the workflow if it helps you finish and inspect real work.
plans.catch: Usage and add-ons can add cost. Generated changes still need review, meaningful tests and release checks.
plans.alternative: Codex or Claude Code if already included in your plan; GitHub Copilot.

plans.name: GitHub Copilot
plans.why: The lower-priced paid coding entry in this selection. A sensible first comparison for someone already using GitHub and a supported editor.
plans.catch: Premium work draws on credits and plan allowances. “AI included” does not mean unlimited use of every model.
plans.alternative: Try the free tier, or compare the coding tools in an existing general plan.

plans.name: Jasper
plans.why: A specialist to evaluate when a team repeatedly needs branded campaign work and a consistent process, not just one clever headline.
plans.catch: The extra subscription needs to earn its place through reusable brand context and workflow. It cannot promise conversion lift.
plans.alternative: A general assistant plus an approved brand brief and editorial checklist.

plans.name: Canva
plans.priceText: Free · paid US price at checkout
plans.why: Useful when the output needs to become a real social post, slide or branded layout. Templates and editing can be more useful than another chat window.
plans.catch: The pricing page localized outside the US during our check, so we do not quote a US price. AI passes or top-ups may add cost.
plans.alternative: Your current design tool plus the image features in a general subscription.

plans.name: Midjourney
plans.why: Our specialist shortlist for visual exploration: compare many moods, compositions and directions before commissioning the final asset.
plans.catch: Stealth is restricted to Pro and Mega. Do not assume a private chat means private generations. Check commercial terms for your use.
plans.alternative: Image generation already bundled with a general assistant.

plans.name: Runway
plans.why: For motion studies, short clips and testing a visual idea before a larger production. Standard includes a credit allowance.
plans.catch: Video iteration spends credits quickly; rejected takes cost something too. Free credits are a one-time allowance, not a monthly production budget.
plans.alternative: A storyboard, still images and your existing editor before paying for generated motion.

plans.name: ElevenLabs
plans.why: A specialist shortlist for narration, voice production and dubbing workflows. Starter includes commercial licensing under its terms.
plans.catch: The $11 Creator offer is first-month pricing, not the recurring price. Credits are shared across products; clone voices only with appropriate permission.
plans.alternative: Record your own voice, or use existing narration tools when the job is simple.

plans.name: Notion AI
plans.why: A candidate when the team’s notes and knowledge already live in Notion. The value is finding and working with that shared context.
plans.catch: Free and Plus offer AI trials rather than the full Business bundle. Confirm billing term, seat count and any additional agent charges at checkout.
plans.alternative: Your current workspace search and an assistant working on selected documents.

plans.name: Zapier Agents
plans.why: Useful when a repeatable task crosses several apps. Start with one observable workflow, such as preparing a draft from a new approved record.
plans.catch: Agent activity allowances, automation tasks and external model costs are different meters. A connected tool can also make a wrong action faster.
plans.alternative: A deterministic automation for predictable steps; add AI only where interpretation helps.

plans.name: Otter
plans.why: A meeting-focused comparison for transcription and turning conversation into follow-up material. Especially useful when missed details create work.
plans.catch: Confirm billing term and regional price before buying. Check minutes and meeting limits, and obtain the recording permissions the meeting requires.
plans.alternative: Meeting notes or transcription already included with your workplace tools.

plans.name: Elicit
plans.why: For literature discovery and structured extraction from research papers. Pro is $39/user/month equivalent, billed $468 annually.
plans.catch: A retrieved paper is not a settled conclusion. Read methods, applicability and limitations before relying on extracted findings.
plans.alternative: General search and a reference manager for lighter research.

plans.name: Harvey
plans.why: A legal-team procurement candidate for specialized knowledge work and workflows. Evaluate it with representative, approved matters and the people who will review output.
plans.catch: No public list price was verified. Ask about seats, onboarding, integrations, data handling and the full contract cost.
plans.alternative: Existing legal research tools; a general assistant only within the firm’s approved boundaries.

plans.name: Spellbook
plans.why: A focused comparison for legal teams drafting and reviewing contracts. Workflow fit can be worth more than buying a second general chatbot.
plans.catch: A seven-day trial is advertised for lawyers and legal teams. Have a qualified reviewer check jurisdiction, citations, obligations and negotiated language.
plans.alternative: Your existing contract tools and approved document assistant; neither replaces legal judgment.

plans.name: Rosebud
plans.why: Our first comparison for reflective use: journaling, spotting your own patterns and preparing to say something clearly to another person.
plans.catch: Treat intimate entries as sensitive data. A useful reflection is not a diagnosis, a therapist’s assessment or knowledge of someone else’s intentions.
plans.alternative: A private journal, a general assistant for low-sensitivity rehearsal, and a real conversation.

plans.name: Replika
plans.why: A companionship product, which is a different purchase from a work assistant. Try only with a clear idea of what you want from the interaction.
plans.catch: Paid prices vary by offer and platform; we do not invent a universal figure. Keep human relationships central and review privacy and recurring billing.
plans.alternative: Journaling or conversation practice; professional support when that is what you need.

plans.name: Khanmigo
plans.why: The low-cost specialist shortlist for guided learning. Teacher tools are free; learner and parent access has separate eligibility rules.
plans.catch: Confirm country and age eligibility. Judge it by whether you can explain and solve the next problem yourself.
plans.alternative: Free Khan Academy lessons or an assistant asked to teach through questions.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.why: A candidate for difficult synthesis, coding and multi-step work when extra reasoning is worth the price. Test the quality gain against cheaper options.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.why: Our OpenAI starting comparison for repeated work: a much lower unit price than Astra. Escalate only the tasks where a stronger result earns the difference.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.why: Anthropic’s premium candidate for demanding tasks. Compare against Opus on your documents and code before paying the higher rate.

models.name: Claude Opus 5.5
models.why: A middle price point in this shortlist for extended work. A sensible comparison when the cheapest model needs too much correction.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
models.why: A lower-cost Claude candidate for a repeatable workflow. Measure acceptance rate and review time, not merely how fast the first answer appears.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.why: The lowest listed unit cost here during its current pricing window. Google lists a doubling to $1.50 input / $7.50 output from January 1, 2027.

models.name: Grok 4.7
models.why: An alternative API candidate with relatively inexpensive output in this set. Current web or X information requires the relevant search tools; it is not automatic knowledge.

areas.name: Marketing
areas.workflow: Turn approved customer research into three campaign directions, then a brief and draft assets.
areas.start: General assistant + brand brief; add Jasper for repeated team workflow.
areas.checkpoint: Check every product claim and measure actual response, not the model’s confidence.

areas.name: Sales & support
areas.workflow: Summarize a permitted call, prepare follow-up options and draft answers from approved documentation.
areas.start: Your existing CRM/workspace assistant before another subscription.
areas.checkpoint: People approve commitments, pricing and outbound messages; track wrong answers.

areas.name: Legal
areas.workflow: Prepare a document inventory, compare clauses and make a question list for counsel.
areas.start: Approved general tools for low-risk preparation; evaluate Harvey or Spellbook for legal-team work.
areas.checkpoint: A qualified lawyer checks jurisdiction, citations, confidentiality and advice. No plan buys a law license.

areas.name: Relationships
areas.workflow: Write what happened, separate observations from assumptions and rehearse a kinder opening.
areas.start: A journal first; Rosebud for a structured reflection habit.
areas.checkpoint: Talk to the person. AI cannot know their motives, replace mutual consent or provide therapy.

areas.name: Research & writing
areas.workflow: Find sources, build an outline, challenge the argument and revise a draft.
areas.start: One general plan; Perplexity for search or Elicit for literature-heavy work.
areas.checkpoint: Read primary sources, verify quotations and keep your own argument.

areas.name: Software & prototypes
areas.workflow: Describe one small behavior, build it, inspect the change and run a meaningful check.
areas.start: Included coding tools first; compare GitHub Copilot or Cursor for editor fit.
areas.checkpoint: Review permissions, dependencies and failure paths before release.

areas.name: Design & imagery
areas.workflow: Explore compositions, make a mood board and translate the selected direction into a layout.
areas.start: Bundled image tools plus Canva; Midjourney for repeated visual exploration.
areas.checkpoint: Check brand accuracy, rights and whether the result actually communicates the idea.

areas.name: Video & audio
areas.workflow: Make a storyboard, test a short sequence and draft narration before production.
areas.start: Runway for motion; ElevenLabs for voice only when those are recurring needs.
areas.checkpoint: Budget rejected takes and editing time; use voices and likenesses with permission.

areas.name: Operations & meetings
areas.workflow: Turn notes into a draft action list or route new records through a repeatable process.
areas.start: Existing workspace tools; Notion, Otter or Zapier for the missing step.
areas.checkpoint: Keep owners, approvals and a visible error log. Automate reversible steps first.

areas.name: Learning
areas.workflow: Ask for a hint, attempt the problem and explain the solution back.
areas.start: Free learning material; Khanmigo for a guided tutoring workflow.
areas.checkpoint: Check understanding without the assistant. Finished homework is not the same as learning.

areas.name: Finance & planning
areas.workflow: Organize your own budget categories and compare explicitly stated scenarios.
areas.start: A spreadsheet and a general assistant, with formulas checked.
areas.checkpoint: Verify arithmetic and assumptions. Use qualified advice for consequential investment or tax decisions.

areas.name: Health preparation
areas.workflow: Organize symptoms and questions for an appointment from notes you choose to share.
areas.start: Your own notes and a general assistant for organization, not diagnosis.
areas.checkpoint: Confirm medical information with a clinician; do not let a chatbot delay urgent care.

areas.name: Hiring & management
areas.workflow: Draft a role brief, prepare consistent questions and summarize job-relevant evidence.
areas.start: Approved workspace tools and a clear rubric.
areas.checkpoint: People make decisions; check bias, sensitive data and applicable employment requirements.

areas.name: Everyday life
areas.workflow: Plan a trip, compare purchases or turn a large household project into a first step.
areas.start: Start free, or use the general plan you already have.
areas.checkpoint: Verify opening hours, booking conditions and prices before spending money.
